answer: Reputation-weighted rate limits. Each identity starts at a nadir of one action per epoch; sustained valid work raises its ceiling along a concave curve, so ten fresh identities yield barely more throughput than one. Cloned identities must each climb that vine separately, paying the full latency cost per clone. Attacker cost scales linearly with identity count while capacity grows sublinearly, making a forge of N sybils cost O(N) time for near-constant output.
